dataset.name: Depth-resolved seasonal porewater chemistry measurements from 3 locations around Meander A of the East River, Colorado.
description: Depth-resolved pore water samples were recovered from 3 locations around Meander A in the East River near Crested Butte, CO, USA for a suite of physiochemical analyses. Supplemental_Information.csv contains water quality measurements including pH, conductivity, temperature, ORP, TDS, O2 concentration, metal concentrations, carbon chemistry, and isotopic signatures; Coordinates.csv contains information regarding sampling locations; and Analysis_Notes.csv contains information regarding instrumentation and detection limits.

measurementTechnique: Samples were collected during base flow (August and October 2016), peak flow (May 2017), and intermediate flow (July 2017). Pore water samples were collected using pore water sippers (MHE drive-point groundwater sippers) inserted into the streambed. These samples were collected at a 10-cm resolution over 70 cm vertical profiles.

Unfiltered pore water samples from 10, 20, and 50 cm depths from each sampling location and season were preserved (refrigerated at 4ºC for 24 hours) for a resazurin-based aerobic respiration assay to track oxygen consumption, which was analyzed using a Horiba Fluoromax 3 spectrofluorometer (Horiba Jobin Yvon Inc. Edison, NJ, USA) (Stern et al., 2017). Base flow characterization of aerobic respiration was performed in October 2016 instead of August 2016 due to limited infrastructure. Filtrate was used in the field for conductivity, ORP, pH, and total dissolved solids using a Myron Ultrameter II Model 6PFCE (Myron L Company, Carlsbad, CA, USA). Dissolved oxygen and sulfide were also quantified in the field using a portable CHEMetrics V-2000 Photometer and Indigo Carmine and Methylene Blue CHEMetrics kits (CHEMetrics, Midland, Virginia).

Splits from each pore water sample were filtered in the field through a 0.22 µm filter, and immediately placed on ice for analysis of solute chemistry. Cr, Mn, Fe, Mn, Hg, Mo, Sr, U, Pb, As, Cu, and Zn concentrations were measured at The Ohio State University’s Trace Element Research Laboratory using inductively coupled plasma ionization (ICP) coupled with optical emission spectrometer (ICP-OES, PerkinElmer Optima 5300DV). Sr isotopic analyses were performed at Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory using a chemical separation technique (Christensen et al. 2007; Christensen et al. 2018) to isolate Sr for isotopic analysis on a Triton Multicollector Thermal Ionization Mass Spectrometer (TIMS) (ThermoFisher Scientific). Changes in aqueous carbon pools in the pore fluids were analyzed using a 21 Tesla Fourier Transform Ion Cyclotron Resonance Mass Spectrometer (FTICR-MS) for the presence/absence of all carbon compounds within a sample at the US Department of Energy Environmental Molecular Sciences Laboratory (EMSL) user facility. Putative chemical formulas were assigned using in-house software “Formularity” (Tolic et al., 2017). FTICR-MS data was used to characterize bulk shifts in carbon classes using molar H:C and O:C ratios which can be grouped into different biochemical classes (e.g., lipids, proteins, amino acids, carbohydrates) using delineations outlined in Kim et al, 2003 and Koch and Dittmar, 2006 (Kim et al., 2003; Koch & Dittmar, 2006).
